Theme

flow verb

also flowing, run (of water), flow away, flow by, flow past, flow down, flow out, flow down from, flow into, flow out from

classical

Varr. LL 5.27
Cic. Div. 1.78: ut flūmina in contrāriās partēs flūxerint (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 204
Traupman 316

1flūxī: long u in the perfect and supine (Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked). De Vaan s.v. fluō, after Weiss (1994), explains flūxī as made by analogy on struō : strūxī, which has a long vowel. The house spelling of the readers (latinitas AGENTS.md §2), with the compounds dēflūxit, efflūxit.

fluō1, fluere, flūxī, flūxum

verb, third conjugation, intransitive

The general word for water, rivers and anything that flows; flūmen, “river”, is made from it.

Other words

  • mānō, mānāre, mānāvī, mānātum — flow, trickle, ooze

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Verg. A. 3.175: gelidus tōtō mānābat corpore sūdor (Lewis & Short)

    Of liquid that seeps or trickles: sweat, tears, blood from the nose.

  • alluō (adluō), alluere, alluī — flow by, wash against

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Leg. 2.6: fluvius latera haec adluit (Lewis & Short); Traupman 204: to flow by, adluere

  • praeterfluō, praeterfluere — flow past

    with the accusative · also used · classical · Lewis & Short: aqua quae praeterfluat, Varr. RR 3.16; Traupman 204

Examples

  • stillicidium eō quod stillātim cadit; flūmen quod fluit continuē

    the drip from the eaves (stillicidium) because it falls drop by drop (stillātim); a river (flūmen) because it flows on and onVarr. LL 5.27

  • īnfīrmō capitī fluit ūtilis, ūtilis alvō

    it flows, good for a weak head, good for the stomachHor. Ep. 1.16.14

  • adluere

    to flow byTraupman 316

  • dēfluere dē

    to flow down fromTraupman 316

  • īnfluere in

    to flow intoTraupman 316

  • effluere ab

    to flow out fromTraupman 316

  • praeterfluere

    to flow pastTraupman 316

See also river, stream, pour, water.
